content: For patients diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, noninsulin injectable therapies such as pramlintide and GLP-1 receptor agonists can play a supportive role in managing blood glucose levels. Pramlintide, which has received FDA approval specifically for use in type 1 diabetes, has been shown to provide modest reductions in hemoglobin A1C levels and body weight. However, it is important to note that pramlintide cannot replace insulin therapy and must be used as an adjunct treatment. GLP-1 receptor agonists, on the other hand, are currently only approved for the treatment of type 2 diabetes. Despite this, clinical studies have demonstrated that these agents may offer some benefits for individuals with type 1 diabetes, including modest reductions in body weight, a decrease in the required insulin dosage, and slight improvements in A1C levels.
